items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: the saxophone player, Edgar Socher was playing that... Edgar was playing, da Just like that, he was doing that years back.

ctx.x: Yeah. Red Island was playing a lot of flatted fifths back in 1929. I got records of that and all that stuff, you know. Higginbotham Blues, the ends of a flatted fifth in 1929. That's what J.C. Higginbotham was playing. He was out of that Louis Russell group, you know.

Well, to say this, in other words, the rock and roll stuff they're playing now, the saxophone player, Edgar Socher was playing that. That's not the one Boogie Woogie or that old time Boogie Woogie? But I mean, the way they're putting that old time stuff in it. Edgar was playing, da Just like that, he was doing that years back. I used to like to hear the blues. Is Kuyper from here? No, Kuyper, not from here. Who is he? That was another trumpet player we had. He had plenty of changes. Nobody had a trumpet player?
